summary: What each `*_status` field in STATUS.yaml claims, typed. STATUS.yaml writes three kinds of statement about a subject into one flat namespace, so eight subjects carry a duplicate key and a YAML reader silently keeps only the last. This file does not repair the prose: it says what the prose means. A reader keeps its own line and gains a subject and a claim kind. It gains no standing: see what_this_types. The same move `contracts/decision-standing.json` already made for decision records.
not_in_scope: Whether a claim is true. This types what is asserted, never whether it holds.
Decision standing. `contracts/decision-standing.json` grades a decision record's settlement; this grades what a status field says about a subject.
Authority. Naming a claim kind grants nothing and settles nothing.
Repairing STATUS.yaml. The file is unchanged by this contract and remains the hand-written record until a projection can regenerate it.
naming_screen: `standing` already carries two senses here - artifact standing (OPEN -> BUILT -> WITNESSED -> RATIFIED) and decision standing. A third would be the collision OPEN-SEAMS.md S20 was closed to prevent, so this contract is named for the field it types (`status`) and now carries no standing of its own at all. No new name is minted; Bdo owns naming (NAMING.md).

STATUS.plain_english: The general state of the subject, as the document's main body records it.

OWNER_ACCEPTANCE.plain_english: The root seat accepted a finished result. `reference` names the packet.

RULING.plain_english: A reversible default taken under decisions/0046. STATUS.yaml's own comment states these are not owner acceptance and do not claim to be.

refusals.ENTRY_MALFORMED: An entry missing a required field or carrying one of the wrong type. Checked first and alone, so a malformed entry is refused rather than raising.
refusals.ENTRY_UNKNOWN_KEY: An entry carrying a key this table does not grade. Closed rather than type-checked: a declared field nothing reads is the defect this table exists to refuse.
refusals.FIELD_UNTYPED: A `*_status` field and value in STATUS.yaml with no crosswalk entry.
refusals.FIELD_UNREADABLE: A line naming a status field the strict reader cannot parse, however it is written - quoted, hyphenated, dotted, in a list item or a flow mapping, at any indent. Anchored on a real `_status` suffix so a bare `status:` key, which no entry could match, is not reported.
refusals.ENTRY_UNMATCHED: A crosswalk entry whose field and value are not in STATUS.yaml.
refusals.SUBJECT_NOT_DERIVED: A subject that is not the field stem with underscores hyphenated. Declaring it freely let a witness dissolve a real collision by renaming one side of it.
refusals.CLAIM_KIND_UNDECLARED: A claim kind outside the three this contract declares. A typo here silently disabled the rule keyed on it.
refusals.CLAIM_KIND_COLLISION: Two entries share a subject and a claim kind. This is the real duplicate the flat namespace could not distinguish from two kinds of claim about one subject, and it also refuses the same field and value typed twice.
refusals.CLAIM_KIND_CONTRADICTS_VALUE: The value's leading tokens and the declared kind disagree. Total in both directions, and tokenised rather than separator-literal, so `RULED-O19` is a ruling.
refusals.REFERENCE_CONTRADICTS_VALUE: An entry names a packet its value does not carry, or carries one it does not name. `reference` is load-bearing for owner acceptance, and a load-bearing field graded nowhere is a declaration.

evolution: 1 - typed crosswalk beside the hand-written file, which is this contract; nothing in STATUS.yaml changes and the eight duplicate keys stop being ambiguous.
2 - a standing change emits a journal entry, so the typed record becomes derivable rather than authored.
3 - STATUS.yaml is regenerated from the journal and the hand-written file becomes a projection. Only then does the file itself change.

refusals_note: Each refusal must be provable alone: selfcheck requires a case to earn exactly the code it names. A refusal that cannot fire without another firing beside it is not a distinct rule.
owner_accepted_reading: Eighteen live values begin `OWNER_ACCEPTED` without a packet digit and are typed STATUS. That follows STATUS.yaml's own comment - `OWNER_ACCEPTED_A*` "names the packet the root seat acted on" - so a bare `OWNER_ACCEPTED_...` value is the document reporting that an acceptance happened rather than the record of the act. A second witness flagged this as possibly a code defect. It is a reading, and it is Bdo's to overturn: if those eighteen are acceptances, the prefix rule and eighteen entries change together.
what_this_types: Which subject a status line is about, and which kind of claim it makes. Not what standing the subject holds: `scripts/sov_standing.py` owns standing claims and checks the thing that decides one, whether a witness record exists naming the subject. Three earlier drafts here extracted a standing from the value's prose and three independent witnesses broke all three - a prose source, then a NOT vocabulary, then word order - each closing the reported instance and leaving the class open in a new spelling. The extraction is removed rather than respelled a fourth time. Reading a structured fact out of unstructured prose was the mistake; a second weaker standing rule beside the one that owns it was also the competing authority AGENTS.md forbids.
closed_key_set: An entry carries exactly field, value, subject, claim_kind, detail and reference. A witness added asserted_standing, settled_by, authority and a resurrected standing_source to live entries and every one passed, because type-checking named keys never rejects an unnamed one. The set is closed: any key outside it is refused, whatever the size of the set.
